_provenance.taxonomy: Kitchener et al. 2017, 'A revised taxonomy of the Felidae', IUCN/SSC Cat Specialist Group, as codified on the Wikipedia 'List of felids' page, which states: 'The following classification is based on the most recent proposals, as codified in 2017 by the Cat Specialist Group of the IUCN.' Cross-referenced with the Mammal Diversity Database.
_provenance.characters: Wikipedia 'List of felids' data table, which sources each species row to its IUCN Red List assessment. Body-length and tail-length ranges in cm, geographic range and habitat are copied verbatim into the source_range / source_habitat fields below.
_provenance.lineages: The page groups the extant genera into eight named lineages: seven in Felinae (Bay cat, Caracal, Ocelot, Lynx, Puma, Leopard cat, Domestic cat) and one in Pantherinae (Panthera).
_provenance.normalisation_note: region_tokens and habitat_tokens are a controlled-vocabulary tokenisation of the verbatim source_range / source_habitat prose in the same row. Tokenisation only splits and lowercases regions and habitats the source already names; it adds no region or habitat the source does not state. The one geographic normalisation applied: the lion row's wording 'India' is tokenised as indian_subcontinent, the token the source itself uses for the tiger and leopard rows.
_provenance.coverage_note: Only body length, tail length, geographic range and habitat are available in the source table. No coat-pattern, dentition, skull or behavioural characters are present, so none are encoded. Where these characters do not uniquely separate two species, the domain under-resolves to the finest shared taxon by design.
